source.title: Understanding Decoupled and Early Weight Decay
source.authors: Johan Bjorck; Kilian Q. Weinberger; Carla P. Gomes

record.tranche_reason: The paper compares weight-decay schedules and sharpness measures against generalization outcomes using a different setting and metric from the listed versions.
record.gate_note: The shuffled-label experiment reports weight norms and test-accuracy curves, but the text does not state random-label test accuracy or establish that the networks fit random labels while generalizing on natural labels. Figures 1–3 and 6–7 have curves without recoverable exact values in the supplied text.
record.test_reason: The multiplicative weight-perturbation experiment tests the magnitude-aware sharpness component of V7 using a different metric and weight-decay interventions. The Adam comparisons do not establish an adaptive-versus-SGD generalization gap or its recovery.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is substantially accurate. The authors argue that early weight decay keeps norms small, increases effective learning rates, and favors minima flatter under multiplicative perturbations. Dataset properties influence norm growth. For Adam, separating objective and decay signals explains decoupled weight decay's tuning stability; sufficiently tuned standard weight decay can match or sometimes exceed its performance.
record.recipe_differences: Tests weight-decay schedules and optimizer decay variants on ResNet/DenseNet image classification, Atari DQN, and translation; uses perturbation sharpness measures rather than the original versions' full set of interventions.
record.method_sensitivity: Weight-decay timing and strength, dataset/game, and sharpness metric change the reported outcome. For DQN, the λ required for standard WD to approach no-WD performance differs across games.

fits_no_version.finding: Hessian, Keskar, and additive sharpness measures give inconsistent or reversed explanations of weight-decay generalization differences.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Sharpness measures sensitive to weight scale can misrank generalization across weight-decay schedules.

fits_no_version.finding: Decoupled weight decay and separate Adam buffers outperform standard weight decay at the recorded Atari coefficient; translation also favors decoupling except at the smallest coefficient.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Separating weight-decay and objective-gradient signals improves Adam's robustness to the weight-decay coefficient.

fits_no_version.finding: Early weight decay keeps norms small; matching those norms by rescaling roughly reproduces its accuracy benefits.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Weight-decay timing affects generalization through weight scale and effective learning rate.

fits_no_version.finding: Weight-norm growth differs between natural and shuffled labels and across Atari environments.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Dataset properties influence weight-norm growth and effective learning rates.

record.problems: Several central comparisons are shown only as curves without exact values in the supplied text. The sharpness comparison is qualitative and does not directly report a training-test gap ranking. Atari table values are averages over three seeds, but no standard deviations are included in the table.
record.rows_left_out: Figure 1 accuracy curves and Figure 3 scaled-weight curves lack recoverable exact values or a textually stated random-label test-accuracy result; no rows extracted for them. Figure 6 curves overlap the Table 1 Atari comparisons and were not added as separate rows. Appendix learning curves for other λ values are figure-only and not included.

untested.parts: No complete paired natural/random-label train/test accuracy comparison is recoverable. Table 2 mentions changing the shuffled-CIFAR-10 learning rate to obtain full training accuracy, so the extraction understates the available memorization evidence; nevertheless, identical recipes and random-label chance-level test accuracy are not established.
No width sweep beyond the width required to fit the training data.
No adaptive-versus-SGD comparison, corresponding training-performance comparison, or demonstration of recovery of an SGD generalization advantage.
No batch-size intervention under fixed epoch budgets.
No dropout intervention; the transformer's fixed dropout setting is not a test.

No direct ranking of training-test error gaps among models established to have similarly low training loss; no perturbation-radius threshold based on training error; no comparison with the specified norm and margin measures. The image experiments use crop and flip augmentation and do not include SVHN.
No removal of examples selected by memorization influence.

missing.what: Figure 2 also compares magnitude-aware perturbation loss across weight-decay schedules for ResNet50 on CIFAR-100 and DenseNet121 on tiny-ImageNet. Its caption reports consistent explanation by multiplicative perturbations across the displayed experiments; these model/dataset conditions need separate rows.
missing.locator: Figure 2 and its caption; experimental setup in On the Temporal Dynamics of Weight Decay

missing.what: Large gamma sometimes prevents the multiplicative metric from distinguishing early and late weight decay for DenseNet121; gamma around 0.1 works across the reported experiments.
missing.locator: Appendix B, Further Experiments, opening paragraph

record.verdict_notes: The study is not an original source for V7. Exact figure values cannot be recovered from the supplied text, but explicit qualitative findings support the limited verdicts. Missing comparisons with norm and margin measures are untested components, not negative results.

versions.untested_parts: The text does not report the paired natural-label and random-label train/test accuracy results needed to test coexistence of memorization and generalization.
No width sweep or test-error comparison beyond interpolation.
No convolutional versus fully connected comparison.

No SGD or momentum-SGD comparison, no language-model benchmark, and no test of broader tuning or switching from Adam to SGD. Results concern Adam-based translation and reinforcement-learning settings.
No batch-size comparison or fixed-epoch large-batch penalty test.

The paper does not compare the measure across the specified one-convolutional-family models on CIFAR-10 and SVHN without augmentation, nor does it report a direct training-test error gap ranking against the listed norm and margin measures.
